compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Nothing in rebar tracks eval spend in dollars. `usage_log.record()` (`src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py`) writes per-call token rows to `.rebar/usage.jsonl` only inside a gate session, `usage_report._price_row` can price rows via the optional `genai-prices` extra, the `rebar metrics` gate-economics lens counts calls not dollars, and there is no aggregate cap anywhere — the only limiter is the per-plan shed budget in `sizing.py`. This epic must stay under $200 on Bedrock, so the cap has to be enforced by the harness, not remembered by people.

## Approach

Build `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/ledger.py`:

- A committed ledger `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/ledger.jsonl`: one row per eval run (`run_id, tier, candidate, sample_n, started, finished, per-pass model ids, input/output/cache tokens, usd, price_table_version`) plus per-call rows in a git-ignored detail file. `cap_usd` and `reserve_usd` are constants in the module (200 / 30).
- **Pre-flight**: each tier computes an estimate from stored corpus token counts × `genai-prices` current prices for the pinned Bedrock model ids; `ledger.reserve(estimate)` refuses (non-zero exit, clear message with remaining allocation) when `spent + estimate > cap − reserve`.
- **Metering**: every eval run opens a usage-log session with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` pointed at a per-run file; on completion the rows are priced and the ledger row finalised with actual spend; a run that dies mid-way is finalised from whatever rows exist on the next `ledger reconcile`.
- `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay ledger` prints spent / remaining / per-tier totals.

Assume `genai-prices` Bedrock ids as the price source; the ledger records the price-table version so later re-pricing is possible.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/ledger.py` (new)
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/ledger.jsonl` (new)
- `pyproject.toml` (the `pricing` extra becomes a dependency of the eval package's entry point)
- `tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_ledger.py` (new)

## Testing

Unit: reserve succeeds under the cap and refuses over it with the remaining amount in the message; a finalised run's usd equals priced tokens; a crashed run is reconciled from partial rows; the cap and reserve are read from one place. No live calls needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every Tier-1/Tier-2 run appears in the committed ledger with actual priced spend and per-pass model ids; checked by the ledger after the commissioning runs.
- [ ] A run whose pre-flight estimate exceeds the remaining allocation is refused before any LLM call; checked by a unit test and by a manual dry-run with an artificially low cap.
- [ ] `ledger` prints spent/remaining and the total never exceeds $200 across the epic; checked at epic close.
- [ ] Unit tests pass in `make test`.
